data.title: Journey of Water
data.introduction: Explore how moisture moves all around our planet through these key terms.

terms.definition: The process where liquid turns into invisible gas when heated by the sun.
terms.exampleSentence: Heat from the sun causes evaporation from the puddle on the sidewalk.
terms.clozeSentence: As the sun warmed the damp towel, slow evaporation made it dry again.
terms.scenario: A wet sidewalk slowly becomes completely dry on a warm and sunny afternoon.

terms.definition: The change of a gas back into liquid droplets when it cools down.
terms.exampleSentence: Cold soda cans develop condensation on their outside surface.
terms.clozeSentence: Tiny droplets formed on the bathroom mirror due to cold condensation.
terms.scenario: Water droplets form on the outside of a cold glass of lemonade on a hot summer day.

terms.definition: Any form of moisture that falls from the sky toward the ground.
terms.exampleSentence: Heavy rain and snow are common types of precipitation.
terms.clozeSentence: Dark storm clouds brought sudden precipitation that ruined our picnic.
terms.scenario: Raindrops and snowflakes begin falling from the gray sky while you walk home.

terms.definition: The gathering of fallen liquid into large areas like lakes and oceans.
terms.exampleSentence: Rivers flow downhill to help with the collection of rainwater.
terms.clozeSentence: Rainwater rushed down the street, ending in a large collection at the storm drain.
terms.scenario: Rainwater flows down the street and pools together into a big puddle.

terms.definition: A substance in the form of a gas that is usually a liquid at normal temperatures.
terms.exampleSentence: Hot tea releases invisible vapor into the cold air.
terms.clozeSentence: Steaming soup sent warm vapor rising toward the ceiling.
terms.scenario: Steam rises up into the air from a pot of boiling spaghetti on the stove.

terms.definition: A visible mass of tiny floating water droplets high in the sky.
terms.exampleSentence: A fluffy white cloud drifted slowly across the blue sky.
terms.clozeSentence: We looked up and saw a gray rain cloud blocking the sun.
terms.scenario: You look up and see a big, puffy, white shape floating high in the sky.

terms.definition: To change from a solid state into a liquid by gaining heat.
terms.exampleSentence: The warm spring sun helps melt the remaining winter snow.
terms.clozeSentence: Hold the ice cube in your warm hand and watch it quickly melt.
terms.scenario: An ice cube left on the kitchen counter turns entirely into liquid water.
